paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Vayera 1:5: “You find that we pray eighteen blessings every day, but they are not all praises of the Holy One, blessed be He: only the first three and the last three. The twelve blessings are all for human needs. Therefore we do not pray eighteen on Shabbos: If someone has a sick person in his house, he recalls it at “Who heals the sick of His people Yisrael” and becomes distressed. Shabbos was given to Yisrael for sanctity, delight, and rest, and not for distress. Therefore one prays the first three blessings, the last three, and rest in the middle. Thus David said, “Seven times a day I praise You”: these are the seven blessings prayed on Shabbos. Which day is this? The one distinctive day, with rest unlike any other, as it is stated: “Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it”—to sanctify it in every matter, even from pursuing your affairs and speaking of them.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:2: ““God blessed the seventh day [and sanctified it]” – Rabbi Yishmael said: He blessed it with manna and He sanctified it with manna. He blessed it with manna in that all the days of the week one omer [of manna] would fall, while on the day before Shabbat two omers would fall. He sanctified it with manna, as it did not fall on it [on Shabbat] at all. Rabbi Natan says: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it with a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it through the gatherer. He blessed it with apparel. Rav Huna said: He should change his clothing. Rabbi Ḥiyya said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: He should mix [garments]. Avin bar Ḥisdai said: He should lower [his garments]. Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Ze’eira were walking together [on Shabbat], and the outer garment of Rabbi Yirmeya was raised up, but Rabbi Ze’eira lowered his. This shows that one should lower [one’s garments for Shabbat]. Rabbi Elazar says: He blessed it with [the Shabbat] candle, and there was an incident involving me [that illustrates this]. One time I kindled a candle on Shabbat eve, and I came and found it burning at the conclusion of Shabbat, and nothing [of the oil] was diminished. He blessed it with the radiance of a person’s face, He sanctified it with the radiance of a person’s face. The radiance of a person’s face all the days of the week is not comparable to the way it is on Shabbat. He blessed it with the lights. Rabbi Shimon bar Yehuda of Kefar Akko says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: Even though the lights were cursed on the day before Shabbat, they were not stricken until the conclusion of Shabbat. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: Adam the first man, his glory did not spend the night with him. What is the source? “Man [adam] will not go to rest in his splendor; he is like the beasts that perish” (Psalms 49:13). The Rabbis say: His glory did spend the night with him, and only at the conclusion of Shabbat was his radiance taken from him, as He expelled him from the Garden of Eden. That is what is written: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). When the sun set on Shabbat eve, the Holy One blessed be He sought to put away the [primordial] light, but He accorded honor to Shabbat. That is what is written: “God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it” – He blessed it with light. When the sun set on Shabbat eve the [primordial] light continued to function. Everyone began praising [God]; that is what is written: “Under all the heavens they sing His praises, and His light is to the ends of the earth” (Job 37:3). Why was this? Because “His light is to the ends of the earth.” Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Simon said: By the light that the Holy One blessed be He created on the first day, a person could look out and see from one end of the world to the other end. When the Holy One blessed be He looked at the people of the generation of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion, whose actions were to be corrupt, He arose and hid it away and designated it for the righteous in the future. From where is it derived that He hid it away? It is as it is stated: “Their light will be withheld from the wicked, and the upraised arm will be broken” (Job 38:15). And from where is it derived that He designated it for the righteous in the future? It is as it is stated: “But the path of the righteous is like a dawning light, growing brighter until the day is established” (Proverbs 4:18). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ze’eira: That [primordial] light functioned for thirty-six hours – twelve on the day before Shabbat, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat. As the sun set at the conclusion of Shabbat, darkness began approaching, and Adam the first man became afraid, as it is stated: “And I said that darkness will envelop me [yeshufeni]; night for me is light,” (Psalms 139:11) – that one [the serpent] in whose regard it is written: “He will strike you [yeshufekha] with his head, and you will strike him [teshufenu] with your heel” (Genesis 3:15), is now coming to confront me. What did the Holy One blessed be He do? He prepared for him two flint stones and he struck them one against the other. Light emerged from them and he recited a blessing over it. That is what is written: “Night for me is light.” What blessing did he recite over it? [Blessed be God] Who creates the lights of fire. This is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel, as Shmuel said: Why does one recite a blessing over light at the conclusion of Shabbat? It is because that time was the beginning of its creation. Rav Huna in the name of Rav and Rabbi Abahu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One recites a blessing over it [light] at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as well, because fire rested all that day.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: תּוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עַל דָּא תָּנֵינָן שַׁבָּת דּוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְאָתֵי אִיהוּ, הָכִי הוּא וַדַּאי, וְעַל דָּא שְׁמִיטָה וְיוֹבֵל דּוּגְמָא דָּא בְּדָא. וְשַׁבָּת וְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי הָכִי הוּא. וְהַהוּא תּוֹסֶפֶת דְּנִשְׁמְתָא מֵרָזָא דְּזָכוּר קָא אַתְיָא עַל הַאי סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם דְּנָטִיל מֵעָלְמָא דְאָתֵי וְדָא תּוֹסֶפֶת יַהֲבַת לְעַלְמָּא קַדִּישָׁא. וּבְהַהוּא תּוֹסֶפֶת חָדָאן וְיִתְנְשֵׁי מִנַּיְיהוּ כָּל מִלִּין דְּחוֹל וְכָל צַעֲרִין וְכָל עָאקִין כְּמָא דְאַתְּ אָמֵר (ישעיהו י״ד:ג׳) בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ יְיָ לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמֵרָגְזֶךָ וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה וְגו'.
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: Rabbi Shimon further said: For this reason we have learned that Shabbos resembles the World to Come. It certainly is so, and for this reason the Sabbatical year and Jubilee resemble one another; so too Shabbos and the World to Come. That additional soul comes from the mystery of “remember” upon this shelter of peace, which takes from the World to Come, and this addition is given to the holy world. In that addition they rejoice, and all weekday matters, all sorrows, and all troubles are forgotten by them, as it is stated: “On the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, from your agitation, and from the hard labor.”

p: וְכֵן נִכְתְּבוּ הַפְּסוּקִים מֵהַסְּעוּדוֹת עַל סֵדֶר הָאָבוֹת (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד
): And in this exact order of the three Patriarchs are written the three clauses of the verse regarding Shabbat (Isaiah 58:14): "
אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'" – לְעוֹנֶג, נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
. 1) "Then you shall delight (tit'anag) upon Hashem" – corresponding to "for delight" (oneg), paralleling the sanctity of Abraham our father. "
וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ" – הַיְינוּ לִמְנוּחָה (נֶגֶד יִצְחָק), דִּכְתִיב: "וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ ה' לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמִרָּגְזֶךָ וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה" (יְשַׁעְיָה יד, ג

), 2) "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth" – corresponding to "for rest" (menuchah, paralleling Isaac), as it is written: "And it shall come to pass in the day that Hashem shall give you rest (haniach) from your sorrow (atzbekha), and from your turmoil (rogzekha), and from the hard bondage" (Isaiah 14:3),
שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א מח רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הָנִיחַ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן נְיָיחָא בַּלֵּב
: which is expounded in the holy Zohar (Part I, 48b top) regarding the Sabbath day, which is the day of rest wherein Hashem, blessed be He, grants tranquility to the heart: "
מֵעָצְבְּךָ" – מֵעֶצֶב הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁנִּקְרָא עֶצֶב, וְהַיְינוּ עַל הֶעָבָר
; "from your sorrow (atzbekha)" – from the melancholy of the evil inclination, which is called sorrow, over what has passed; "
וּמִרָּגְזֶךָ" – מֵרוֹגֶז הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְהַבָּא, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ה.): "לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע

"; "and from your turmoil (rogzekha)" – from the agitation and provocation of the evil inclination regarding the future, akin to the expression (Berakhot 5a) "A person should always incite (yargiz) the good inclination against the evil inclination"; "
וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה" – הַיְינוּ שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת
. "and from the hard bondage" – referring to the subjugation of foreign regimes.
וְזֶהוּ "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ" – הַיְינוּ שֶׁתִּרְכַּב וְתִשְׁלוֹט עַל חִשְׁקֵי וְתַאֲווֹת אֶרֶץ הַגְּבוֹהִים (כִּיבּוּשׁ הַיֵּצֶר, מִדַּת יִצְחָק

), And this is the meaning of "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth"—that you shall ride above and master the haughty cravings and earthly lusts (the conquest of the evil inclination, which is the Gevurah of Isaac),
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ עַל שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח.) מִדִּכְתִיב: "וְאַתָּה עַל בָּמוֹתֵימוֹ תִדְרֹךְ" (דְּבָרִים לג, כט), וְזֶהוּ לִמְנוּחָה

. and in the Gemara (Shabbat 118a) it is likewise expounded as freedom from the subjugation of the nations, from the verse "And you shall tread upon their high places" (Deuteronomy 33:29); and all of this constitutes true rest (menuchah). "
וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ" – הַיְינוּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה, שֶׁמִּדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הוּא הַדְּבֵיקוּת בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

: 3) "And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father" – corresponding to "for holiness" (kedushah), for the attribute of Jacob our father is cleaving (deveikut) to Hashem, blessed be He: "'
קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ' – הֱיוּ קְדוֹשִׁים כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֲנִי קָדוֹשׁ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים, וְהַיְינוּ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

; as in "'You shall be holy, for I Hashem your God am holy' (Leviticus 19:2) – be holy just as I am holy," as expounded in Midrash Tanchuma, Parashat Kedoshim, which signifies the sacred union of the Holy One, blessed be He (Tiferet / Jacob), and Knesset Yisrael (Malchut);
וְזֶהוּ "נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב" – שֶׁמַּמְשִׁיךְ כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הֲוָיָ"ה לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא "שְׁלִימוּ דַּאֲבָהָתָא" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְנוּ (בְּמַאֲמָר ב
). and this is "the heritage of Jacob," who channels the entire sanctity of the Tetragrammaton into Knesset Yisrael, being the "perfection of the Patriarchs" as we explained above (in Discourse 2).

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Yitro 27:455-457: “Rabbi Elazar said to his father: “How are these meals arranged?” He said to him: “Of Shabbos night it is written, ‘I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth.’ On that night the Matron is blessed, together with the whole field of apples. A person’s table is blessed, an additional soul is given, and that night is the Matron’s joy. A person must rejoice in her joy and eat the Matron’s meal. On Shabbos day, at the second meal, it is written, ‘Then you will delight above Hashem’—‘above Hashem,’ precisely. At that hour the Holy Ancient One is revealed, and all the worlds are joyful. We bring about the completeness and joy of the Ancient One, and it is certainly His meal. At the third meal of Shabbos it is written, ‘I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father.’ This is the meal of Zeir Anpin, who is in completeness, and all six days are blessed from that completeness. A person must rejoice in his meal and complete these meals, which are the meals of the complete faith of Israel’s holy seed, who possess the supernal faith. They belong to them, and not to the idolatrous nations. Therefore He said, ‘Between Me and the Children of Israel.’””

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְאָבוּי, אִלֵּין סְעוּדָתֵי הֵיךְ מִתְתַּקְנִין. אָמַר לֵיהּ, לֵילְיָא דְּשַׁבְּתָא, כְּתִיב, וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ. בֵּיהּ בְּלֵילְיָא, מִתְבָּרְכָא מַטְרוֹנִיתָא, וְכֻלְּהוּ חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין, וּמִתְבָּרְכָא פָּתוֹרֵיהּ דְּבַר נָשׁ, וְנִשְׁמְתָא אִתּוֹסְפַת, וְהַהוּא לֵילְיָא, חֶדְוָה דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא הֲוֵי. וּבָעֵי בַּר נָשׁ לְמֶחדֵי בְּחֶדְוָותָא, וּלְמֵיכַל סְעוּדָתָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא. בְּיוֹמָא דְּשַׁבְּתָא, בִּסְעוּדָתָא תִּנְיָינָא, כְּתִיב (ישעיהו נ״ח:י״ד) אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל יְיָ'. עַל יְיָ' וַדַּאי. דְּהַהִיא שַׁעֲתָא אִתְגַּלְיָא עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא, וְכֻלְּהוּ עָלְמִין בְּחֶדְוָותָא, וּשְׁלִימוּ וְחֶדְוָותָא דְּעַתִּיקָא עַבְדֵּינָן, וּסְעוּדָתָא דִּילֵיהּ הוּא וַדַּאי. בִּסְעוּדָתָא תְּלִיתָאָה דְּשַׁבְּתָא, כְּתִיב וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ. דָּא הִיא סְעוּדָתָא דִּזְעֵיר אַפִּין, דְּהַוֵי בִּשְׁלֵימוּתָא. וְכֻלְּהוּ שִׁיתָא יוֹמִין, מֵהַהוּא שְׁלִימוּ מִתְבָּרְכָן. וּבָעֵי בַּר נָשׁ לְמֶחדֵי בִּסְעוּדָתֵיהּ, וּלְאַשְׁלְמָא אִלֵּין סְעוּדָתֵי, דְּאִינּוּן סְעוּדָתֵי מְהֵימָנוּתָא שְׁלֵימָתָא, דְּזַרְעָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּי מְהֵימָנוּתָא עִלָּאָה, דְּהָא דִּילְהוֹן הִיא, וְלָא דְּעַמִּין עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת. וּבְגִינִי כַּךְ אָמַר, (שמות לא) בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: Rabbi Elazar said to his father: “How are these meals arranged?” He said to him: “Of Shabbos night it is written, ‘I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth.’ On that night the Matron is blessed, together with the whole field of apples. A person’s table is blessed, an additional soul is given, and that night is the Matron’s joy. A person must rejoice in her joy and eat the Matron’s meal. On Shabbos day, at the second meal, it is written, ‘Then you will delight above Hashem’—‘above Hashem,’ precisely. At that hour the Holy Ancient One is revealed, and all the worlds are joyful. We bring about the completeness and joy of the Ancient One, and it is certainly His meal. At the third meal of Shabbos it is written, ‘I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father.’ This is the meal of Zeir Anpin, who is in completeness, and all six days are blessed from that completeness. A person must rejoice in his meal and complete these meals, which are the meals of the complete faith of Israel’s holy seed, who possess the supernal faith. They belong to them, and not to the idolatrous nations. Therefore He said, ‘Between Me and the Children of Israel.’”

: However, in the holy Zohar (Yitro 88b), the clauses of this verse are assigned to the three Sabbath meals in a different order:

בִּסְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת כְּתִיב: "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ", וּבִסְעוּדָתָא תִּנְיָנָא (בַּבֹּקֶר): "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'", וּבִסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית כְּתִיב: "וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ

". at the Friday night meal (corresponding to Isaac/Gevurah) it places "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth"; at the second meal on Sabbath morning (corresponding to Abraham/Chesed) it places "Then you shall delight upon Hashem"; and at the third meal (corresponding to Jacob) it places "And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father."
וְהָעִנְיָן, שֶׁמִּצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַסֵּדֶר הוּא "אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" (מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה) וְאַחַר כָּךְ "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" (לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה

) – The explanation of this difference is that from the perspective of Hashem, blessed be He (from above to below), the order begins with "I am Hashem your God" (the root of positive commandments, Chesed) and is followed by "You shall have no other gods" (the root of negative prohibitions, Gevurah)—

); for at the utterance of "I am," Torah study was implanted in their hearts, and at the utterance of "You shall have no," the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts, as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (on "Let him kiss me");

p: וְכֵן כָּאן, מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַסֵּדֶר הוּא לִזְכּוֹת תְּחִלָּה בְּלֵיל שַׁבָּת לְ"וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ" – שֶׁהוּא הַנְּיָיחָא מֵעֶצֶב וְרוֹגֶז הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁהוּא שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה, וּמִמֵּילָא נִיצּוֹל מִשִּׁעְבּוּד

; So too here: from the side of Israel's upward progression through the Sabbath meals (in the Zohar), the order begins on Friday night with meriting "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth"—which is resting and breaking free from the sorrow and agitation of the evil inclination (the leaven in the dough) and from foreign subjugation ("turn away from evil");

וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת: "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'" – שֶׁהוּא לִזְכּוֹת לִבְחִינַת עֹנֶ"ג (רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת: עֵדֶן, נָהָר, גַּן), "לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחְמִי" (מִשְׁלֵי ט, ה), לִזְכּוֹת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עוֹנֶג מֵעֵדֶן עִלָּאָה, וְזֶהוּ "בֵּרְכוֹ בַּמָּן" שֶׁהוּא לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
. and afterward on Sabbath morning one ascends to "Then you shall delight upon Hashem"—attaining the level of
עֹנֶג

(an acronym for Eden, Nahar River, Gan Garden), "Come, eat of My bread" (Proverbs 9:5), meriting the delight of Torah from the supernal Eden ("and do good"), which corresponds to "He blessed it with the manna," the bread from heaven.

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּישַׁעְיָה, שֶׁנִּסְדַּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁבָּא הַשָּׂכָר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "אָז תִּתְעַנַּג" תְּחִלָּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ", כְּסֵדֶר "אָנֹכִי" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "לֹא יִהְיֶה

". In contrast, in the verse in Isaiah, which is ordered according to how the reward flows down from Hashem, blessed be He, "Then you shall delight" comes first and is followed by "And I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth," matching the divine order of "I am" followed by "You shall have no."
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נַפְשׁוֹת הָאָבוֹת, נוֹלַד מִתְּחִלָּה אַבְרָהָם וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִצְחָק
; Similarly, when Hashem, blessed be He, brought the souls of the Patriarchs into the world, Abraham (Chesed) was born first and afterward Isaac (Gevurah);
וּבִסְעוּדוֹת שַׁבָּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנֶּחְשָׁב כְּנֶגְדָּן, נֶחְשָׁב מִקּוֹדֶם סְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת נֶגֶד יִצְחָק וְאַחַר כָּךְ סְעוּדַת יוֹם שַׁבָּת כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם

, whereas in the Sabbath meals of Israel which parallel them (and just as in the cycle of the day, night precedes day), the Friday night meal corresponding to Isaac comes first, followed by the Sabbath daytime meal corresponding to Abraham,
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא הַסֵּדֶר מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹת וּלְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לִזְכּוֹת לִקְדוּשַּׁת הָאָבוֹת
. in accordance with the upward order through which Israel must strive to attain the sanctity of the Patriarchs.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:2: ““God blessed the seventh day [and sanctified it]” – Rabbi Yishmael said: He blessed it with manna and He sanctified it with manna. He blessed it with manna in that all the days of the week one omer [of manna] would fall, while on the day before Shabbat two omers would fall. He sanctified it with manna, as it did not fall on it [on Shabbat] at all. Rabbi Natan says: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it with a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it through the gatherer. He blessed it with apparel. Rav Huna said: He should change his clothing. Rabbi Ḥiyya said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: He should mix [garments]. Avin bar Ḥisdai said: He should lower [his garments]. Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Ze’eira were walking together [on Shabbat], and the outer garment of Rabbi Yirmeya was raised up, but Rabbi Ze’eira lowered his. This shows that one should lower [one’s garments for Shabbat]. Rabbi Elazar says: He blessed it with [the Shabbat] candle, and there was an incident involving me [that illustrates this]. One time I kindled a candle on Shabbat eve, and I came and found it burning at the conclusion of Shabbat, and nothing [of the oil] was diminished. He blessed it with the radiance of a person’s face, He sanctified it with the radiance of a person’s face. The radiance of a person’s face all the days of the week is not comparable to the way it is on Shabbat. He blessed it with the lights. Rabbi Shimon bar Yehuda of Kefar Akko says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: Even though the lights were cursed on the day before Shabbat, they were not stricken until the conclusion of Shabbat. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: Adam the first man, his glory did not spend the night with him. What is the source? “Man [adam] will not go to rest in his splendor; he is like the beasts that perish” (Psalms 49:13). The Rabbis say: His glory did spend the night with him, and only at the conclusion of Shabbat was his radiance taken from him, as He expelled him from the Garden of Eden. That is what is written: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). When the sun set on Shabbat eve, the Holy One blessed be He sought to put away the [primordial] light, but He accorded honor to Shabbat. That is what is written: “God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it” – He blessed it with light. When the sun set on Shabbat eve the [primordial] light continued to function. Everyone began praising [God]; that is what is written: “Under all the heavens they sing His praises, and His light is to the ends of the earth” (Job 37:3). Why was this? Because “His light is to the ends of the earth.” Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Simon said: By the light that the Holy One blessed be He created on the first day, a person could look out and see from one end of the world to the other end. When the Holy One blessed be He looked at the people of the generation of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion, whose actions were to be corrupt, He arose and hid it away and designated it for the righteous in the future. From where is it derived that He hid it away? It is as it is stated: “Their light will be withheld from the wicked, and the upraised arm will be broken” (Job 38:15). And from where is it derived that He designated it for the righteous in the future? It is as it is stated: “But the path of the righteous is like a dawning light, growing brighter until the day is established” (Proverbs 4:18). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ze’eira: That [primordial] light functioned for thirty-six hours – twelve on the day before Shabbat, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat. As the sun set at the conclusion of Shabbat, darkness began approaching, and Adam the first man became afraid, as it is stated: “And I said that darkness will envelop me [yeshufeni]; night for me is light,” (Psalms 139:11) – that one [the serpent] in whose regard it is written: “He will strike you [yeshufekha] with his head, and you will strike him [teshufenu] with your heel” (Genesis 3:15), is now coming to confront me. What did the Holy One blessed be He do? He prepared for him two flint stones and he struck them one against the other. Light emerged from them and he recited a blessing over it. That is what is written: “Night for me is light.” What blessing did he recite over it? [Blessed be God] Who creates the lights of fire. This is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel, as Shmuel said: Why does one recite a blessing over light at the conclusion of Shabbat? It is because that time was the beginning of its creation. Rav Huna in the name of Rav and Rabbi Abahu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One recites a blessing over it [light] at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as well, because fire rested all that day.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 119a:7: “With regard to the wealthy of other countries, where there are no Sages, by what virtue do they merit their wealth? He said to him: Because they honor Shabbat, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: One time I was hosted at the home of a homeowner in Laodicea and they brought before him a table of gold that was so heavy it required sixteen people to carry it, and there were sixteen chains of silver attached to it, and there were bowls and cups and pitchers and flasks attached to it, and there were all sorts of food, and delicacies, and fragrant spices on it. And when they placed it there they would say: “The earth and all that fills it is God’s, the world and all that inhabit it” (Psalms 24:1). ; Now in the Torah's account of Shabbat in Vayekhullu (Genesis 2:2-3), the order is: first "And He rested (vayishbot) on the seventh day"—which is rest (menuchah);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי" – שֶׁהוּא "בֵּרְכוֹ בַּמָּן" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יא, ב), וְהַיְינוּ עוֹנֶג שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֵדֶן נָהָר גַּן
and second, "And God blessed (vayevarekh) the seventh day"—which is "He blessed it with the manna" as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (11:2), representing delight (oneg: Eden, Nahar, Gan) (
וְכֵן כְּתִיב: "בִּרְכַּת ה' הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר" [מִשְׁלֵי י, כב], וְנִדְרַשׁ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם: זוֹ הַשַּׁבָּת
, (and similarly it is written: "The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich" Proverbs 10:22, which is expounded in Bereishit Rabbah there as referring to Shabbat,

וְהָעוֹשֶׁר בָּא עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָה וְעוֹנֶג לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שָׁם מֵהַטַּבָּח, וְשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְעוֹשֶׁר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם וּבַגְּמָרָא שַׁבָּת קיט

.); for wealth comes through eating and delighting to honor the Shabbat, as illustrated in the Midrash Rabbah there by the story of Joseph who honored Shabbat and inherited the pearls of the hatmaker/butcher, and as taught in the Gemara, Shabbat 119a, that the wealthy merit riches because they honor Shabbat);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ" – לִקְדוּשָּׁה
. and third, "and He sanctified it (vayekaddesh oto)"—corresponding to holiness (kedushah).

, The reason why Vayekhullu places "And He rested" (menuchah) before "And He blessed" (oneg) is that there "And He rested" speaks primarily of Hashem, blessed be He, experiencing satisfaction and rest in His completed world, which found favor in His eyes, as stated in Midrash Rabbah;
רַק מִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה גַּם הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִנְיָיחָא – "נוּחוּ בֵּיהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנָחִי בֵּיהּ אֲנָא
". and as a natural consequence of His resting, Israel likewise merits rest: "Rest on it just as I rested on it."

But there is another path for a great and holy person, who is ashamed to ask for his body's closeness, as it says, “I am dust and ashes.” By sitting at the entrance, casting aside his body and soul, he longs only to fulfill his Creator's will. Similarly, on the holy Shabbos it is written, “From pursuing your own affairs.” Because an additional illumination is revealed on the holy Shabbos, a person should forget his bodily affairs, and only a request for rest and “Purify our hearts” was instituted. Yet, as a consequence, a person who is remembered before Hashem certainly has, as it is written, “No lack for those who fear Him.” Consequently, when a person has someone who is ill, the sick person is also healed through Shabbos prayer, even though he does not pray for him. This is the meaning of visiting the sick: from the inner point, life and healing are drawn to all things rooted there.”

Similarly, on the holy Shabbos it is written, “From pursuing your own affairs.” Because an additional illumination is revealed on the holy Shabbos, a person should forget his bodily affairs, and only a request for rest and “Purify our hearts” was instituted. Yet, as a consequence, a person who is remembered before Hashem certainly has, as it is written, “No lack for those who fear Him.” Consequently, when a person has someone who is ill, the sick person is also healed through Shabbos prayer, even though he does not pray for him. This is the meaning of visiting the sick: from the inner point, life and healing are drawn to all things rooted there.”

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְסַיֵּים בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא שָׁם: "אֵלּוּ שֶׁבַע בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין בְּשַׁבָּת. וְאֵיזֶה זֶה יוֹם הַמְּיוּחָד וְהַמְּנוּחָה שֶׁאֵין כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ? זֶה הַשַּׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי

", And afterward the Midrash Tanchuma concludes there: "These correspond to the seven blessings that we pray on Shabbat. And which is this unique day and rest unlike any other? This is the Shabbat, etc."
וְלֹא זָכַר כָּאן מִשְּׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת שַׁבָּת רַק הַמְּנוּחָה
. Here at the conclusion, out of the three dimensions of Shabbat, the Midrash mentions only "rest" (menuchah).
וְהַטַּעַם, שֶׁבְּפָרָשַׁת "וַיְכֻלּוּ" נִזְכַּר רַק "בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי", וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרָא הַיּוֹם בַּתּוֹרָה בְּשֵׁם "שַׁבָּת" (עַל שֵׁם "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת
"), The reason is that in Vayekhullu the day is initially called only "the seventh day," and subsequently throughout the Torah it is named "Shabbat" (after vayishbot, "and He rested"),
שֶׁהָעִיקָּר מַה שֶּׁנִּיתַּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא הַשְּׁבִיתָה בְּשַׁבָּת
; because the foundational mitzvah commanded to Israel in the Written Torah is the cessation of labor (shevitah) on Shabbat;
שֶׁמִּצְוַת עוֹנֶג לֹא בָּא בַּתּוֹרָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַק בְּרֶמֶז בִּתְלָתָא "הַיּוֹם", וְעִיקָּרוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי קַבָּלָה ("וְקָרָאתָ לַשַּׁבָּת עֹנֶג

"), whereas the mitzvah of delighting (oneg) on Shabbat is not stated explicitly in the Pentateuch, appearing only by way of allusion in the three occurrences of "today" (ha-yom) and articulated explicitly in the Prophets ("And you shall call the Shabbat a delight" Isaiah 58:13);
וְנִקְרָא הַיּוֹם רַק עַל שֵׁם הַמְּנוּחָה – "שַׁבָּת", שֶׁהוּא "נוּחוּ בֵּיהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנָחִי בֵּיהּ אֲנָא
". and therefore the day itself is named strictly after rest—"Shabbat"—which is "Rest on it just as I rested on it."
